definitions.explanation: Grapes that have been dried, either in the sun or by other methods. A common snack and baking ingredient in Japan.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}しぶどう{入|い}りのパン。
サラダに{干|ほ}しぶどうを{加|くわ}えた。
examples.english: I added raisins to the salad.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}しぶどうは{鉄分|てつぶん}が{豊富|ほうふ}で、おやつとしても{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Raisins are rich in iron and popular as a snack.

notes:
Composed of {干|ほ}し (dried — from {干|ほ}す, to dry) + ぶどう ({葡萄|ぶどう}, grapes). A straightforward compound following the common Japanese pattern of {干|ほ}し + food name for dried foods.

USAGE:
The English loanword レーズン is also very common in Japan and may be more frequently used in commercial and culinary contexts (especially baking). {干|ほ}しぶどう is the native Japanese term and is understood by everyone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}しぶどう{入|い}り — containing raisins
- {干|ほ}しぶどうパン — raisin bread
- {干|ほ}しぶどうを{入|い}れる — to add raisins

SIMILAR WORDS:
- レーズン — raisin (English loanword; common in recipes and product names)
- ぶどう — grape (fresh, not dried)
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき} — dried persimmon (another traditional Japanese dried fruit)
